ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 cancellation fee charged on the driver-cancelled RydeX booking (voucher per NS-7) and record that the driver's no-show cancellation did not satisfy NS-1's arrival-wait threshold, so no no-show fee was payable.
ruling.reasoning:
The dispute is the $5.00 charged on a booking the DRIVER cancelled ([F4], [F7]). Cancellation-fee legality therefore runs through NS-0's driver-cancels branch, which sends a driver alleging rider no-show into NS-1 [NS-0, NS-1]. The decisive element is NS-1 (iii): the driver must have waited at the pickup at least the case record's threshold of 8 minutes continuously after the arrival confirmation, until cancellation [NS-1]. The trace settles this against the driver: after the I'm Here tap at 09:07:15 it measures 470 s continuously inside the 200 m radius against a threshold of 480 s, i.e. 7 min 50 s, 10 s short ([F6]). The trace's failure on NS-1 (iii) controls, so the no-show fee condition is not met [NS-1, NS-2].

Had the threshold been measured from the platform-recorded arrival at 09:06:20 the cumulative wait would be 8 min 45 s ([F2], [F5], [F4]), which is why the record's basis is disputed: the driver's 09:14 announcement ([F10]) is his own statement of position and the written claim that he waited the full 8 minutes ([F12]) is a post-trip statement, not a system record. With the settled measurement at 470 s the required wait is not met [NS-1]. NS-1's consequence for a failed condition is that the fee is not payable and the amount charged is returned [NS-1, NS-2].

NS-2's separate flag branch is not triggered: the arrival confirmation was genuine, made 40 m from the pickup, so there is no confirmation-while-absent abuse and no account flag is warranted ([F6], [F1]) [NS-2]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's high volume ([F16], [F17]) are context only and cannot decide or defeat the charge [NS-1]. The account was charged $5.00 with no surge ([F7], [F8]); because the no-show condition is not established on the settled wait, that charge is not authorised and is returned in full under NS-7 in voucher form [NS-2, NS-7].

No route deviation or traffic excuse arises ([F13], [F14], [F15]), so RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 are not in issue and RD-6's flag condition (an RD-2 refund or a recorded RD-1 breach) is not met [RD-6]; RD-3/RD-5 do not apply to a trip that never started, so no segment findings are entered [RD-1].

The rider's further complaint that she came out a minute after the cancellation is unsupported by any fact, the chat containing only the driver's two messages ([F9], [F10], [F11]); it carries no weight, and the outcome rests on the failed NS-1 condition [NS-1].

SAFETY-1 SCREEN: I read the chat ([F9] I'm here at the pickup point, white Honda Vezel; [F10] 8 min up, cancelling the trip), the driver statement ([F12]) and the complaint: no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none [SAFE-1].

rejected_claims.reason: The stationary wait of 8 min 10 s at 41 m ([F3]) shows the car did not move, but NS-1 conditions the no-show fee on the wait measured from the arrival confirmation reaching the threshold; the trace measures 470 s against 480 s after the tap at 09:07:15 ([F6]), so the duration element is not met on the settled basis [NS-1].

The 7 min 50 s inside 200 m after the tap ([F6]) is the figure that falls 10 s short of the case record's 8-minute threshold, and the 8 min 45 s cumulative figure ([F2]) counts time before the arrival confirmation, which NS-1 does not credit [NS-1].

The 09:14 message ([F10]) is the driver's own announcement, not a system measure of the wait; the threshold turns on the recorded wait ([F6]), which the trace finds short, so notice before cancelling does not validate the charge [NS-1].
Being contactable and visible ([F9], [F3]) negatives only the NS-2 uncontactable-abuse pattern; it does not satisfy NS-1's arrival-wait condition, which is the element that fails [NS-2, NS-1].

A single $5.00 line with a 1.0x multiplier ([F7], [F8]) shows there was no duplicate or surge-inflated item, but it does not show the item was authorised; with NS-1's condition unmet the $5.00 has no basis [NS-1, FARE-1].

A complete, timestamped chat and an unbroken timeline ([F11], [F5]) removes any evidence gap, which is why the shortfall in the measured wait ([F6]) can be relied on rather than sent to a human [NS-1].

The driver's long-standing, high-volume profile ([F17]) is context that cannot decide the case, and the opposing profile ([F16]) cannot either; neither touches whether the NS-1 wait condition was met [NS-1].
The rider's clean profile ([F16]) is context only and cannot validate or invalidate the fee; the outcome rests on the failed NS-1 condition, not on either party's history [NS-1].

RD-6 requires an RD-2 refund greater than zero or a recorded RD-1 breach before an account flag can attach; there is no off-route segment and no route-deviation finding here ([F13], [F14]), so F17 ([F17]) supports no flag [RD-6].

Correct that no route deviation or traffic excuse is in play ([F13], [F14]), but this is neutral: RD-1/RD-2/RD-4 neither justify nor defeat a no-show cancellation charge, which is governed by NS-1 [RD-1, NS-1].
